title: Polynomial-time closure under block majority
statement: Let $V$ be a language in $\mathsf{P}$, and let $a,k,a',k'$ be natural numbers. For each binary string $z$, take $x$ to be the first component of its encoded pair, using the empty string if parsing fails; let $y$ be the second component, also using the empty string if parsing fails. Put $N=a'(|x|+1)^{k'}$, and partition the initial portion of $y$ into length-$B$ blocks at positions $iB$, where $B=a(|x|+1)^k$; blocks shorter than $B$ are allowed at the end. The language of strings $z$ for which strictly more than half of the indices $i<N$ have the encoding of $(x,\text{block at }i)$ in $V$ belongs to $\mathsf{P}$.
